criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: The deck is bold. Fields are dark, light pools from the low west key, and the cover's bunk and steers run off three edges. The weaknesses repeat across frames. The kit Hereford on 1, 6 and 8 reads as a toy: smeared hide, no hair, a blobby muzzle, blue-grey legs. On 8 that model fills about 60% of the frame. Slide 2's bunk sits in a thin band at y 1080 to 1340 of 2000, with about 250 px of dead dark above it and a similar strip below the labels. Slide 3 is a flat diagram with no world. Slide 7's page is an unshaded cream slab, and machine QA flags it as 'top-loaded composition ... dead lower zone'. Slides 4 and 6 put type on dark plates (the two pen labels on 4, the URL pill on 6). The 9 figure is a stiff mannequin.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: One world: a Panhandle feedyard at last light. The key is computed from the sun at 259 degrees and 6.1 degrees elevation, and shadows run long to the east on 1, 5, 6 and 9. One precast bunk and galvanized rail run from the cover to the close, and the storyboard declares MOTIF_EVOLUTION and CAMERA_MOVE. The dusk-gold accent is held to the tag on 1 and 8 and the rule on 7. Slide 3 is a flat 2D grid map and sits outside the rendered stock. Slide 7's bright page is the deck's one value jump.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces. 9.75, 4.875 and 19.5 come from c1 and c3. 135, 22 percent, 2.47, 2.32, 11.2 and the 500 thousand drawing rule are all in figures.json via compute.py. The slide 7 sentence matches c6 word for word, and the slide 3 squares measure true. Four things are looser than their sources. (1) Slide 6's headline does not name its set: the NASS rows cover only feedlots of 1,000 or more head, and only the dek says 'large feedlots'. The lead over Nebraska is 30 thousand head on a survey estimate. (2) 'USDA counted' calls a NASS estimate a count. (3) Slide 3 puts the Kuhlman gift on the ranch's south edge, and no claim gives a direction. (4) Slide 6's dek states a 5-of-22 steer encoding the frame doesn't show legibly. All sources are primary.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened, who got it and where. The AI stake rests on one 'can be evaluated' sentence (c6), so the AI half is a topic more than a story. Slide 9 asks 'Which tool, and what result?' but gives no date, filing or contact a reader could use. By design no county is named.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover hook earns the swipe, and slide 2 pays at once with the money. The turn on 7 lands. Slide 6 is context that could be cut without loss. Slide 8 restates 7's absence rather than moving it on.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and on register, with real Panhandle specifics. 'USDA pays half. The match pays the rest.' is good. 'The grant is awarded. The AI approaches are a plan.' on 9 reads machine-flat. 'drawn to illustrate' appears in eight of nine deks and becomes a tic.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The subject is new: cattle and agriculture. The angle is not: 'the release names no tool or result' is the same move as nos. 46, 47 and 48. The last-light world repeats from nos. 46 and 48. The area-as-a-square device on 3 repeats no. 45. A person at the close is a recurring end.

one_sentence_fix: Replace the kit Hereford with a detailed steer model lit from camera left by the 6.1 degree west key. That one asset is the hero of frames 1, 6 and 8, and its toy look is what holds the artwork score down across the deck.

artwork_weakest_frames.change: The toy-looking kit steer owns about 60% of the frame and its legs run down into the footer. Swap in a detailed steer mesh, rake the face from camera left with the west key, and crop at head and dewlap so the bunk lip and the gold windrow fill the lower third.

The bunk takes up only about 13% of the frame height under about 250 px of dead dark. Move the long-lens camera in and drop the eye to about 0.6 m so the four sections stand about a third of the frame tall across the full width. Seat the brackets directly under the lit lip.

The page is a flat, unshaded cream rectangle and machine QA flags a dead lower zone. Turn the page 15 to 20 degrees into the west key, shrink it to clear the footer, and bring the bunk throat and the grimed back wall into the lower third as planned.

The far steers fall into the fog as one dark mass and the URL sits on a dark plate. Pull the stage fog back until every head separates, light the five behind the divider as one group, and reframe so the bright bunk wall clears the footer and the plate can go.
This is the only unrendered frame. Render the one-mile grid as a dark caliche ground plane under the lastLight key, with the ranch and the gift as low raised slabs casting long east shadows.
